suggestions.quote: Scientists gave 160 teams thousands of facts about thousands of families and asked them to predict how the children's lives would turn out; the best models were only slightly better than a simple guess from four facts (c24).
suggestions.fix: Scientists gave a hundred and sixty teams thousands of facts about thousands of families and asked them to predict how the children's lives would turn out; the best models were only slightly better than a simple guess from four facts (c24).

suggestions.quote: Then the one fact: phone records from fifty thousand people showed where a person will be, hour by hour, is in principle guessable up to about ninety-three per cent of the time, and nobody fell below eighty (c09).
suggestions.fix: Then the one fact: phone records from fifty thousand people showed where a person will be, hour by hour, is in principle guessable up to about ninety-three per cent of the time, and nobody fell below eighty per cent (c09).

keep.quote: in 2008 brain scans could guess whether a person would press a left or right button a few seconds before they felt they'd chosen (c04), and the guess was right about sixty times in a hundred, against fifty for a coin (c05).
when scientists watched people choose where real charity money would go, the famous early brain signal was missing (c06).
An economist put it in 1975: lean on a number to control people, and the number stops behaving (c18).
